newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mulpha eyes board of Interport.
newsitem.headline: Mulpha eyes board of Interport.

text.p: Malaysia's Mulpha International Bhd wants board representation at Philippine firm Interport Resources Corp to justify its substantial stake, the national Bernama news agency said on Tuesday.
"As a substantial shareholder we should, under normal conditions in any company, have board representation," Mulpha chief executive and chairman John Wong Peng Chong was quoted as saying.
Mulpha's 30 percent unit in the Philippines, Mabuhay Holdings Corp, owns a 46.3 percent stake in property firm Interport.

Speaking after Mulpha's annual meeting, Wong said the company was unhappy with a recent rights issue which Interport proposed in the Philippines without notifying Mulpha, an international trading company.
Interport said the issue was to fund property development and administrative expenses.

The matter was referred to the Philippines' Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), which allowed the company to proceed with the issue on condition that the proceeds be deposited with an authorised bank under an escrow and trust account.
"The (firm's) management did not consult us," Wong told reporters. "We are obviously not very happy with the situation and are continuing to pursue the matter via normal channels.
"I would not want to comment too much on this as it may prejudice our position," he added.
Mulpha officials were not immediately available to confirm the Bernama report.
